title: The Marlow Bakery
brief: Marlow's Bakery suspects its bookkeeper, Simon Crale, has been padding the expenses. He inflated four entries in the ledger and pocketed the difference. The TOTAL figures show where the ledger and the bank disagree. Work out which entries he cooked.
clues: Exactly four entries were changed, and every change made an expense bigger.
Rent is fixed by the lease: £800 every month.
The dairy delivers the same order every month, so the dairy bill never changes.
The van was off the road for most of May, so May had the lowest fuel bill of the five months.
story: Crale padded April's wages by £300, then added £120 each to February's flour, March's dairy and May's fuel: £660 in all, paid to himself as "petty cash". The dairy bill gave March away, since it never changes, and May's fuel bill was far too high for a van that never left the garage.
